mercury.vtkjs.title: Mercury
mercury.vtkjs.text:
Magnetic Field: The cutout slices, shows the strength of the magnetic field around Mercury. Studying the slices, particularly looking at the view from the Y-axis, shows how the solar wind is pushing the magnetic field, dragging it away from the planet and creating the tail-formation, knows as the magnetotail. The plasma wake - the region of less dense plasma on the night side of the planet, is also illustrated by the weaker magnetic field seen behind the planet, seen along the X-axis going towards -X.

IMF and Solar Wind: In the model, under B field streamlines and solar velocity streamlines, we seen two components of the solar wind illustrated. The former, showcases the interplanetary magnetic field lines (IMF), generated by the Sun, bending around the planet due to Mercury’s intrinsic magnetic field. The solar wind direction is seen by the velocity streamlines as they the bulk velocity of the solar wind.

Bow shock: The bow shock, the region that forms due to the solar wind meeting an obstacle in the planetary magnetic field, can be seen represented by the voxel cone that shows the particle density around Mercury. The bow shock, is an area where the plasma gets highly compressed, meaning the particles bunch up in the region. Therefore, the bow shock can be represented by the particle density.
